articles.summary: Time series deployments rarely grow the way they were planned. A single-node pilot becomes a multi-node fleet, an afternoon’s worth of test data becomes weeks of backfill that has to land before anyone can query it, and three teams end up writing to a database built for one. InfluxDB 3.11 delivered a higher-performance foundation for complex time series workloads, with significant performance improvements for single-series queries, schemas that could go wide and sparse without breaking, and a much more predictable resource profile. For InfluxDB 3 Enterprise, 3.12 builds on that foundation with more ways to scale operations around those workloads. Bulk imports make better use of available CPU, compaction can now scale across nodes, and schema enforcement gives teams more control over shared production datasets. The common thread is simple: as the workload grows, more of the system can grow with it. Bulk import, now 3x faster Historical data isn’t useful until it’s queryable. When you’re migrating to InfluxDB or backfilling months of history, import speed decides how soon that data sits alongside your live data, whether that’s by lunch or next week. InfluxDB 3.12 makes bulk import from Parquet roughly three times faster. Imports now run in parallel, so they scale with the hardware you give them. In testing, import time fell by 64-70 percent across workloads. Imports are also easier to lock down. Bulk import no longer requires an admin token. It now authorizes against write permission on the target database, so the credential running a backfill only needs access to the data it’s loading. Distributed compaction, now in beta Compaction keeps queries fast by organizing newly written data into efficient files in the background. At high ingest volumes, though, that background work can become the bottleneck: compaction falls behind, and the only fix is a bigger machine. InfluxDB 3.12 removes that ceiling. With distributed compaction, now in beta, compaction becomes something you can scale horizontally. When compaction needs more capacity, add nodes running in compact mode, and the coordinating node spreads jobs across them. If a compact node drops out mid-job, the work is simply reassigned in the next scheduling cycle. Distributed compaction is off by default, so existing deployments behave exactly as they do today. When you’re ready to scale past a single compactor, you can turn it on. Schema enforcement, per database Schema-on-write is one of the things that makes InfluxDB easy to start with: send data, and the schema takes shape around it. But in a production database shared by several applications, that flexibility cuts both ways. A typo in a field name or an unexpected column from one service quietly becomes part of the schema, and every team querying that database has to work around it. InfluxDB 3.12 lets you lock the schema down where it matters. Define the schema when you create a database, and writes that introduce undefined columns are rejected instead of changing the schema. Bad data gets caught at write time, before it reaches dashboards, queries, or downstream consumers. Schema-on-write remains the default, so you can enforce schemas on the databases that production depends on and keep exploratory databases as flexible as ever. More control in the Explorer UI The Explorer UI has a set of updates to keep pace with the teams using it. InfluxDB 3.12 makes role-based access control generally available in InfluxDB 3 Enterprise, so teams can manage access by user and role instead of tracking individual tokens. Users can sign in with a token, a password, or SSO, and using Explorer, admins can manage users and their roles from the same place they query. Explorer also adds six visualization types: area, single stat, gauge, pie, scatter, and ranking. Explain in SQL shows what a query is doing, which makes it easier to check before you rely on it. articles.summary: Employee Management HR Spotlight: Prudence Duru on Hiring Right and Keeping New Hires Engaged Great Goodness Ufford October 1, 2026 Our first HR Spotlight features Prudence Duru, Talent Acquisition & Employer Branding Manager, currently leading employer branding, talent acquisition, and employee lifecycle at SecureID Limited. Her career makes the case that people are an organisation’s most valuable investment. At Eazipay, we believe how people are hired, onboarded, and led shapes how a business grows—which is why HR Spotlight exists: to hear how the people responsible for it actually think. Why She Chose HR Prudence studied Industrial Relations and Personnel Management before the field was called Human Resources. In 2013, during an internship at a government parastatal, she worked in the Employee Relations and Staff Welfare Department. Two moments from that internship stayed with her. The first was managing staff training, including a group sent abroad in December who came back requesting a wardrobe allowance—a request that sounded bizarre to her at the time, until she understood why it wasn’t. The second was less lighthearted. The organisation had no HMO in 2013, so employees covered their own health bills and brought back proof of payment for reimbursement. Before any bill was paid, Prudence had to call the hospital to confirm the employee had been treated there and spent the amount claimed, without the hospital ever disclosing the employee’s condition. Watching how HR related to employees during that first job sparked a curiosity that became a career. She was already equipped for Talent Acquisition; she just didn’t know. She still finds the same thing satisfying today—closing a role with someone who performs well, knowing she supported them through the entire process. The Three Questions Prudence Asks Before Opening Any Role Prudence’s turning point came from a mind-shift. As an in-house recruiter, she stopped seeing recruitment as sourcing CVs and started seeing it as a business function—one that shapes who an organisation becomes. Her scope grew from there, across employer branding, employee lifecycle, performance management, talent acquisition, and workforce planning. That shift changed what she’s responsible for—not just finding candidates, but making the company desirable to commit to, while making sure the people she hires want it just as much. Looking at the full employee journey, from hire to exit, she asks three questions before hiring begins: “Why is this role open? Is this the role we need right now? Should we get a senior person, or an entry-level person we train up?” The Leadership Lesson: Reading the Room Before the Resolution Fairness, clarity, and consistency don’t require treating everyone the same way. It requires adjusting your approach. Early in her career at a previous company, an employee issue was escalated to HR. While the team was still working to understand the circumstances, the employee had an outburst during the conversation. Prudence was scared and shocked, but she came to realise the employee was carrying more than she’d let on. Their intentions were good—understand what happened, work toward a resolution, but the approach still didn’t land the way they hoped. That experience left her with a lesson she still leads by. You have to understand where someone’s head is before you address the issue itself. It’s not about reading body language for its own sake. It’s about creating the conditions for an honest conversation. A resolution reached before that groundwork is laid rarely holds. What “The Right Environment” Actually Looks Like Prudence believes most people want to do well and that they will, given the right environment, the right tools, and clarity on what they’re meant to do. That belief is built into how she runs onboarding. Her KPI, New Hire Experience, exists to measure exactly that. When a candidate has a month-long notice period, she sends the offer letter early and stays in close communication through the gap. Every new hire has what they need on day one—workstation, laptop, and an assigned buddy. New hire induction runs for three days, where they meet heads of every department and learn how their role connects to, and depends on each other. HR then runs its own induction into company culture and values. This involvement continues through the probationary period. The goal: new hires who know why they were hired, who to turn to when they need help, and what their KPIs are, while enjoying the experience. “People deliver their best work when the conditions are built for it.” — Prudence Duru Who Prudence Is Outside of HR Outside of work, Prudence is family-oriented and enjoys the simple things—music, good food, and time with people she cares about. She’s learned to protect her 8-to-5 and leave work at work. That boundary came from a hard lesson in exhaustion. There was a stretch where she left the office late, went to bed late, and woke up drained—until she realised the answer was simple; she wasn’t sleeping enough. The moment that defined her decision was leaving the office once at 10pm. Home was close enough to make that possible, but the cost outweighed the convenience. Since then, she has set firm boundaries around her time—evenings and weekends included. She stays curious about life, and says she discovers something new about herself every day. The Thread Through All of It Every answer Prudence gives points at the same thing: people do their best work when the systems around them are built with intention—the right hire, the right onboarding, the right conversation at the right moment. That’s the same conviction behind how Eazipay approaches payroll and workforce management: the operational backbone should be handled with precision, so HR leaders like Prudence can spend their attention where it matters most—on people. Your STG balance may temporarily not appear in your portfolio during the merger period while the conversion is being processed. Eligible holdings will subsequently be credited as ZRO. When will I receive my ZRO? ZRO balances will be credited to eligible users on or before 11 October 2026. What if I already hold ZRO? Your existing ZRO holdings are not affected by this merger. articles.summary: SmartHelio、初の日本訪問 変わりゆく太陽光発電市場を現地で見て、聞いて、学ぶ これまで1年以上にわたり、日本のお客様とはオンラインを中心にやり取りを重ねてきました。そして今年9月、ついに日本を訪れ、直接顔を合わせてお話しすることができました。 SmartHelioにとって初めてとなる今回の日本訪問では、Photon Capital、NTTアノードエナジー、ENEOSリニューアブル・エナジー、Voltaiyoの皆様とお会いし、実際に私たちの製品をご利用いただいている皆様の声を直接伺いながら、今後について意見を交わしました。 お客様とのワークショップに加え、大阪で開催された Swiss-Japan Energy Days、千葉で開催された Smart Energy Week Japan にも参加しました。今回の訪問を通じて、新たな段階を迎えつつある日本の太陽光発電市場と、その未来を形づくる人々について、より深く知ることができました。 お客様と直接お会いして 今回の訪問では、お客様とのワークショップが中心となりました。 GAIAの最新機能をご紹介するだけでなく、現場で実際にどのような課題を抱えているのかを直接伺うことを大切にしました。 話題はすぐに具体的な内容へと広がりました。アラームだけでは気づきにくい発電ロスの把握、データ確認やレポート作成にかかる時間の削減、そしてBESSの普及に伴う運用の変化などです。また、新しい技術を導入する際には、既存のO&M業務に負担を増やすのではなく、自然に組み込めることが重要だという声も伺いました。 こうした話からも、日本市場の変化が見えてきました。FITを中心に成長してきた市場が次の段階へ進む中、発電性能、運用コスト、プロアクティブなO&M、そして長期的な資産価値の重要性が高まっています。 私たちが改めて感じたのは、日本市場にそのまま「コピー＆ペースト」できる正解はないということです。GAIAも、日本の現場やチームの働き方に合ったものでなければなりません。今回いただいた声を、これからの製品開発に直接つなげていきます。 ワークショップを離れて すべての会話が会議室の中で行われたわけではありません。東京でのランチや、お客様とご一緒した日本料理の席など、特に印象に残る会話のいくつかは、食事を囲みながら生まれました。 1年以上にわたり、画面越しに一緒に仕事をしてきた皆様と、ようやく直接お会いし、オンライン会議ではなかなかできない交流を深めることができました。 2つのイベント、2つの視点 お客様とのワークショップに加え、今回の訪問では、日本のエネルギー業界を異なる角度から知ることができる2つのイベントに参加しました。 大阪 Swiss-Japan Energy Days 大阪でのSwiss-Japan Energy Daysから、私たちの日本訪問は始まりました。研究者や大学関係者から、電力会社、大手企業まで、エネルギー業界の幅広い方々と直接交流する機会となりました。Govindaはエネルギーの未来についての議論に参加し、駐日スイス大使ともお会いしました。そしてOhjiにとっては、SmartHelioを紹介する初めてのピッチとなりました。 千葉 Smart Energy Week その1週間後、千葉でSmart Energy Weekに参加しました。招待制の交流会では、日本のエネルギー業界をリードする方々とお会いする機会をいただき、その後3日間にわたり、ブースで太陽光、BESS、O&M、アセットマネジメントに携わる多くの方々とお話ししました。現場が今抱えている課題や、市場がこれからどのように変わっていくのかを直接聞くことができました。 大阪では日本のエネルギー業界をより広い視点から見ることができ、千葉では現場により近い声を聞くことができました。 どちらも、オンライン会議だけでは得られない、人と直接会い、学ぶ機会となりました。 資産の「監視」から「運用」へ 日本の太陽光発電市場：FITから発電性能重視へ 1. これまで：FITが支えた市場の成長 福島第一原発事故以降、FIT制度による支援を背景に、日本では太陽光発電の導入が急速に拡大しました。当時は、発電所を建設し、安定した収益を確保することが優先され、現在ほど発電性能の最適化は重視されていませんでした。 2. 見えてきた課題 高度なデータ分析の活用はまだ発展途上にあり、O&Mはこれまで、小さな発電ロスや劣化、故障の初期兆候を捉えることよりも、停止や大きな故障への対応が中心となる傾向がありました。 アセットマネジメントの重要性も高まっています。…

articles.summary: SYSTANE PRO Preservative-Free Demonstrates Clinically Comparable Dry Eye Symptom Relief to MIEBO (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution) in a Prospective, Randomized Clinical Study sandra.hoffer Thu, 10/01/2026 - 15:27 Friday, October 2, 2026 SYSTANE PRO Preservative-Free (PF) demonstrated non-inferiority to MIEBO^ (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution) in relieving dry eye symptoms at two weeks and one month1,* Findings provide Eye Care Professionals with comparative clinical evidence supporting SYSTANE PRO PF for patients with dry eye1 FORT WORTH, October 2, 2026 — Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced new investigator-initiated clinical data demonstrating that SYSTANE® PRO Preservative-Free (PF), an Alcon brand, provided clinically comparable dry eye symptom relief to MIEBO^ (perfluorohexyloctane ophthalmic solution), meeting the study's primary endpoint of non-inferiority at both two weeks and one month based on Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) scores.1,* The findings were presented at the American Academy of Optometry 2026 Annual Meeting (AAO; Anaheim; September 30-October 3). “These results provide Eye Care Professionals (ECPs) with meaningful comparative evidence when considering treatment options for patients with dry eye disease,” said Anna Tichenor,*** OD, PhD, FAAO, Assistant Professor and Chief of the IUSO Dry Eye Clinic, and lead investigator of the study. “Based on these findings, I can confidently recommend SYSTANE PRO PF as a first-line treatment option for patients in my practice with dry eye symptoms, particularly given the clinically comparable dry eye symptom relief to prescription perfluorohexyloctane demonstrated in this study. For ECPs with patients facing cost or insurance-related access barriers, Systane Pro PF may offer an accessible approach to dry eye symptom relief.” Dry eye disease (DED) is one of the most common ocular surface disorders, affecting an estimated 39 million people in the United States and 1.6 billion globally.2,3 Common symptoms can include dryness, irritation, burning and fluctuating vision, which can interfere with everyday activities such as reading, night driving, using digital devices, working and socializing.4-6 DED can also affect contact lens wear and may impact a patient’s ability to undergo cataract or refractive surgery.4-6 Yet only 13% of patients with DED feel their condition is well-managed, underscoring the need for effective treatment options that can help address the diverse needs of people living with dry eye disease.7,† This head-to-head study*** was a prospective, randomized, double-masked, multicenter clinical study that evaluated 256 dry eye patients with moderate-to-severe symptoms.1 Patients were randomized to SYSTANE PRO PF or perfluorohexyloctane four times daily in both eyes and were assessed at baseline, two weeks and one month.1 The primary endpoint evaluated non-inferiority of SYSTANE PRO PF versus perfluorohexyloctane on OSDI symptom scores, using a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 7.3 units.1 SYSTANE PRO PF demonstrated clinically meaningful dry eye symptom relief while proving to be non-inferior to perfluorohexyloctane.1,* Both treatment groups achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in OSDI symptoms (p≤0.001) at two weeks and sustained through one month.1,* SYSTANE PRO PF is available over the counter (OTC) in the U.S., Canada and other markets. MIEBO^ is available by prescription in the U.S., while perfluorohexyloctane is offered OTC in certain markets outside of the U.S. “These findings underscore the strength of SYSTANE PRO PF, backed by a rigorous, independently conducted randomized clinical study.” said Sarika Sood, Vice President of Global Medical Affairs and Health Economics and Outcomes Research at Alcon. “The results add to the growing body of evidence supporting SYSTANE PRO PF and reinforce the strength of Alcon’s comprehensive dry eye portfolio.” SYSTANE PRO PF is formulated to provide sustained hydration, restore tear film stability†† and protect against further irritation of dry eyes.8,9 To learn more about Alcon’s dry eye offerings, visit systane.myalcon.com .
